rss.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
rss.summary: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
rss.text_excerpt:
From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently ⁠ (opens in a new window) , predictor) on a very large corpus of data. 1 I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared ⁠ (opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts. A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “ an alien mind ⁠ ”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation. The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset. 2 , 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5. The range of capabilities of models that are largely described by this one metric is stunning. rss.title: How Public Evals Work and Fail, and What Should Change
rss.summary: How to read eval scores and what to question, from a teardown of 12 benchmarks.
rss.text_excerpt:
As models ship faster, eval scores are often the first thing we learn about a new model. But how much weight should we put in them? In eight of twelve public evals studied, there’s evidence the grader failed work that should have passed. And even when the grader gets it right, many benchmarks measure what’s easy rather than what matters, and should instead focus on reliability, work velocity, multi-turn collaboration, etc. Here, we’ll cover the common patterns and principles, the errors models make, and where current benchmarks fall short. I’ll also share what we’re getting wrong and what should change, including why average pass rate isn’t enough and why dollars are the wrong measure of cost. Finally, we’ll walk through twelve evals: four on coding and science, six on knowledge work, and two on browsing and computer use. By the end, you’ll know what to trust in a benchmark and what to question. Patterns: How eval tasks are built and maintained # Most eval tasks share four components: Instruction: A prompt that sounds like a real user’s request. The agent gets it once at the start and typically can’t ask clarifying questions. Environment: The workspace where the agent operates. Typically comes with the files, software, and services needed. For coding, this is usually a container with a repo at a specific git commit. For knowledge work, it might be a VM with installed software, simulated business apps, or a folder of documents. Grader: This decides whether the work passes. It can be deterministic code (tests and assertions over the final output or environment state), an LLM judge scoring a rubric of yes/no criteria, or a mix of both. Reference (optional): A human expert’s solution. Evals include this to prove a task is solvable, anchor pairwise comparisons, or establish a human baseline. The four basic components of an eval task In addition, eval benchmarks are increasingly maintained like software. They ship versioned releases and accept fixes through issues and pull requests. Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 retired 30 tasks and revised 57 others, and Harvey LAB’s public set has grown from about 1,250 tasks to 2,010 since launching in May 2026. Like software, these releases can also introduce breaking changesâTerminal Bench can drop saturated tasks with each version, making scores hard to compare across releases. rss.title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
rss.summary: Proving software correct with math has traditionally required specialist work. Now AI and Lean are helping automate the process.
rss.text_excerpt:
The word of the year in the AI industry over 2026 has been “slop” — meaning low-quality output from a large language model. And with so much code being AI-generated now, avoiding slop has become a daily concern for software engineers. So how to do that? One way is to use formal verification systems , which use mathematical proofs and logic to verify the correctness of software or hardware. How formal verification is used in software and AI today In order to better understand the landscape of formal verification systems, we spoke to one of its leading proponents: Clark Barrett , &Truth’s co-founder and co-CEO. He’s also Corbel Professor (Research) of Computer Science at Stanford and was the co-creator of cvc5 , a popular automated reasoning engine used in formal verification. Without getting too in the weeds, cvc5 is what’s called a “solver” for satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) , which Barrett says is widely used in companies like Amazon. For instance, cvc5 is used for specification analysis and test generation in Kiro , Amazon’s agentic development environment. “It's been fun to see my tools go from a good idea in the lab to cvc5 is now called billions of times a day in production pipelines at Amazon,” Barrett told us. When AI coding agent companies talk about “verifying” their work, it typically means agents running tests, critiquing their own output, or having another AI model judge it. So I asked Barrett how far short of real verification does that fall? “The main difference is really just, how do you know when you're done,” he replied. “So if you're testing, patching, scanning — using all these existing tools — they're quite good. rss.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
rss.summary: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
rss.text_excerpt:
As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly. Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards. An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections. For instance, an adversary might distill a model’s cyber capabilities and use the resulting model to help carry out cyberattacks that the original model would have refused to assist with or that its safeguards would have blocked. We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry. Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities. These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity. We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought. These traces can contain information the final answer leaves out, making them especially valuable training data for another model. W e’ve strengthened our defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol. In an internal adaptive evaluation using strong automated red-teaming , we tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier prompt. The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards. Distillation is a common machine-learning technique in which one model learns from data produced by another. For example, a model can learn from another model’s answers, its reasoning, or its judgments about which answers are better and why . # Coding2API [![CI](https://github.com/RobbsLuo/Coding2API/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/RobbsLuo/Coding2API/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/RobbsLuo/Coding2API)](https://github.com/RobbsLuo/Coding2API/releases) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/RobbsLuo/Coding2API)](LICENSE) [![Image](https://img.shields.io/badge/image-ghcr.io%2Frobbsluo%2Fcoding2api-blue)](https://github.com/RobbsLuo/Coding2API/pkgs/container/coding2api) 把十路渠道——**CodeBuddy**（国内 / 国际两个独立渠道）、**TRAE SOLO**、**OpenCode Zen**、**Kilo**、**Qoder**、**CodeArts**、**OfficeAce**、**小浣熊**、**灵犀**——外加可选的**通用 OpenAI 兼容上游**，封装成 OpenAI 兼容 API：公共凭证池、统一模型名与调度、按人用量统计。 > [!WARNING] > 逆向接口，仅供学习研究，未做安全审计；公网部署需反向代理 + 鉴权 + IP 白名单。 ## 特性 - **多协议出口**：`/v1/chat/completions`（流式 / 非流式）、`/v1/responses`（Codex CLI）、`/v1/messages`（Claude Code）、`/v1beta/models/{m}:generateContent`（Gemini SDK）、`/v1/models`、`/v1/user/balance`、内置检索 `/v1/tools/search` + `/v1/fetch`。 - **统一调度**：扁平名按健康度选号，`模型@渠道` 强制。优先级：免费渠道 → 在途最少 → 到期额度 → 健康度 + 分级冷却 → 余额多者。凭证**权重**（`-1000..1000`）只在同一健康档内重排；目录里的 x0 会被最近 24h 实测扣费校准。模型级限流只避让该模型；多轮对话粘同一凭证，出错才轮换。 - **到期额度优先**：主窗口（默认 36h）先烧将过期额度，打平再比 7 天窗口；单位统一积分。 - **模型列表按凭证加载**：只列有可用凭证的渠道 → 无幽灵模型。目录落盘，重启即用。 - **公共凭证池**：admin 维护、全员共享、`APP_SECRET` 加密入库；设备码 / OAuth 登录、多账号切换、额度探测、签到、token 预刷新。 - **三角色**：`admin` / `operator` / `viewer`（SQLite）；一次性激活链接、首登强制改密、改角色 / 停用即时吊销会话；登录与写操作留审计。 - **成长中心**（仅 CodeBuddy）：领礼、派 Buddy、领任务奖、断登补登、连登兑换、开盲盒。`GROWTH_IRREVERSIBLE_ACTIONS=false` 关停不可逆动作；企业版账号自动跳过。 - **脱敏统计**：不存对话；明细 90 天、小时汇总永久；按人 / 渠道 / 模型 / 凭证可视化；成本按 OpenRouter 刊例价估算；明细走 SSE。 - **月度账单**（`operator` 起）：按月按人 / 按 Key 汇总请求、token 与成本；CSV / JSONL 导出并写审计。 - **工具调用健壮性**：`id` 缺失按 index 补并记忆；DeepSeek DSML 泄漏回读成结构化调用；非流式坏 `arguments` fail-closed（400，不冷却凭证）。 - **失败分流**：`11134` 供应商过载按排队语义（不罚号）；请求级错误换号后不搬会话粘性；全池耗尽 503 带 `Retry-After` 与**池子成因拆解**（`total=25 cooling=20 disabled=3 …`）。 - **加固与运维**：登录限流 / CSRF / 请求体上限 / Host 白名单；出口 IP 粘性（`CREDENTIAL_PROXY_POOL`）；可选出站隐私脱敏（`PRIVACY_RULES`，只改出站副本）；上游状态聚合（只解释不调度）；侧栏待办角标；Prometheus `/metrics`。 - **窄屏适配**：<768px 表格转卡片，DOM 不变。 协议层（私有信封、签名、门禁伪装）见 [`TECHNICAL.md`](TECHNICAL.md)。 ## 界面预览 管理台（截图取自本地实例，账号 / IP 已脱敏）： | 凭证管理：池概况与渠道分组 | 用量统计：请求 / token / 成本 | |---|---| | ![凭证管理](assets/screenshots/credentials.webp) | ![用量统计](assets/screenshots/stats.webp) | | **Playground：模型 × 渠道与倍率** | **模型列表：OpenRouter 刊例价与能力分** | | ![P

![吸星大法 · Skill Siphon](assets/banner.svg) # 吸星大法 · Skill Siphon **吸纳众 Skill 之长，凝练识见以明判** **隔空吸纳、汇入经脉、炼化内力、凝成精华** [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-8B7CF6?style=flat-square&labelColor=221440)](LICENSE) [![Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent_Skills-Compatible-brightgreen?style=flat-square&labelColor=221440)](https://agentskills.io) [![Runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runtime-Multi--Runtime-blue?style=flat-square&labelColor=221440)](#-安装) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/JL-GUO/skill-siphon?style=social)](https://github.com/JL-GUO/skill-siphon/stargazers) **中文** · [English](README_EN.md) [它做什么](#-它做什么) · [工作原理](#-工作原理) · [安装](#-安装) · [用法](#-用法) · [蒸馏尺度](#-蒸馏尺度一个实例) · [诚实边界](#-诚实边界) · [贡献](#-贡献)
--- > 📚 收藏了几百个 skill，真正学到手的有几个？ > 🌟 高星 skill 里写满了门道，读完却只记住几句口号？ > 🎯 想入门一个新领域，不知道先看什么、凭什么判断好坏？ **吸星大法**是一枚 Agent Skill：把优秀 skill 里可学习的工作经验吸纳进来，凝练成你**能理解、能练习、能用上**的学习资料——学会这项工作怎样做、为何这样做、怎样判断好坏，以及情况变化时如何调整。判断力，包含在实际工作能力之中。 ``` 一个领域 / 一个高星 skill → 搜索与选择 → 深读技能源 → 凝练核心经验 → 三份学习资料 → 你的判断力 ```
* * * ## ✨ 它做什么 给它一个**学习目标**，它去吸纳该领域有分量的 skill，列出 3–5 个有区别的候选等你选定；给它一个**明确的 skill**（名称 / 路径 / 链接），它直接开卷深读。然后沿引用读到经验真正成立的位置，把步骤背后的门道、取舍和例外凝练出来，转成新手学得懂、用得上的资料。 > **它不是什么** > > - ❌ 不是 skill 安装器——分析技能源 ≠ 执行它的安装与外部操作指令 > - ❌ 不是资料搬运工——不逐条换词复述原指令，只凝练会改变做法、结果或判断的内容 > - ❌ 不是速成承诺——不许诺一次阅读就拥有高手的全部本领，能力要靠应用和反馈形成 ## 🧠 工作原理 ![工作原理](assets/workflow.svg) | 阶段 | 关键问题 | 对应模块 | |---|---|---| | 1️⃣ 确定学习对象 | 学谁？凭什么选它？ | [find_skills.md](references/find_skills.md) | | 2️⃣ 读到经验成立处 | 门道藏在哪些文件、哪些分支里？ | SKILL.md 第二节 | | 3️⃣ 凝练核心经验 | 哪些内容会改变行动？取舍丢了吗？ | [distillation.md](references/distillation.md) | | 4️⃣ 转成新手能懂 | 术语翻译了吗？案例走得通吗？ | [teaching.md](references/teaching.md) | | 5️⃣ 生成三份资料 | 学什么、怎么练、来源在哪 | [deliverables.md](references/deliverables.md) | | 6️⃣ 检查并交付 | 来源可追？读者能行动？文件可用？ | SKILL.md 第六节 | ## 📦 交付产物 默认三份 Markdown，写入你指定的位置（未指定时为当前工作区 `学习输出/{主题}/`）： | 文件 | 应包含的实质内容 | |---|---| | **01_学习指南.md** | 学什么、适合谁、需要什么最少基础；核心经验、具体做法、理由、取舍、常见错误与合格标准 | | **02_上手实践.md** | 一个规模可控的完整演示；有内容的示范产物；可迁移到自己任务的工作表与检查工具 | | **03_来源与边界.md** | 选定来源、热度口径与日期、阅读范围、核心经验出处，以及重要修正、教学补充和资料缺口 | 内容短小可合并，复杂合集按连贯主题拆分；不为每个经验新增一个文件。需要 Word / PDF 时按可用工具转换。 * * * ## ⚡ 安装 ### 🤖 给 Agent 的一句话安装 装好后直接告诉你的 agent： ``` > 从 https://github.com/JL-GUO/sk [TRUNCATED]

github.text_excerpt:
Put good practice to work.

Open-source practice feedback for software teams

App · Docs · Self-host · Discussions

Hephaestus helps software teams put good engineering practices into their everyday work. It reviews pull requests, issues, code reviews and team discussions as the work happens. Each person gets feedback that cites their work and names a next step. Feedback appears on the work while it is still open, in a weekly digest, and on each person's Practice profile. The profile shows how each practice develops over time. Work drafted with a coding agent gets the same feedback. In a conversation, anyone can ask Hephaestus why, ask for an example, or disagree.
